docs.title: mr01sam Rust Plugins
docs.text:
Documentation for Rust Oxide/Carbon plugins.

Pick a plugin from the sidebar to view its configuration, permissions, and commands.

docs.title: Safe Pocket
docs.text: Gives players a small, death-safe storage pocket. Items kept in the Safe Pocket are not lost when the player dies.

docs.title: Carbon vs. Oxide
docs.text: Safe Pocket is built for Carbon and developed there first. It also runs on Oxide via the Carbon Aliases extension, which is required if you're on Oxide. Some features may not work or may be slower to receive updates on Oxide.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Permissions are not fixed — they're dynamically created from the Permission Tier Overrides section of the config. Each tier you define there gets its own permission (if Auto-Register Permission is enabled for it), so the list below is just what ships by default, not the full set of permissions the plugin can have.

Out of the box:

Permission Effect safepocket.1slot Grants 1 pocket slot. safepocket.2slot Grants 2 pocket slots. safepocket.3slot Grants 3 pocket slots. safepocket.3slot.all Grants 3 slots with every item category allowed (overrides the default resource/component/misc-only restriction).

Add, remove, or rename tiers in the config to change this list — grant a player any tier's permission and the plugin will register it and apply that tier's settings automatically. When a player qualifies for more than one tier, the one with the highest Priority wins.

docs.title: Default Settings
docs.text:
Baseline settings used for any player who doesn't hold a permission from Permission Tier Overrides below.

Key Default Description Permission Required null Not set on the default tier — it's the fallback everyone gets. Auto-Register Permission true Whether the plugin should auto-register this tier's permission. Slot Count 0 Number of pocket slots granted. 0 disables the Safe Pocket entirely for that tier. Open Delay (seconds) 3 Seconds the pocket takes to finish opening. 0 opens instantly. Priority (higher wins when multiple tiers apply) 0 Resolution priority. Allowed Item Categories ["Resources", "Component", "Misc"] Item categories that can be placed in the pocket. Item Blacklist (shortnames) [] Item shortnames always rejected, regardless of category.

docs.title: Permission Tier Overrides
docs.text: A list of tiers, each gated behind its own permission. Any field left unset on a tier falls back to the matching value in Default Settings. Add as many tiers as you want — these keys are the same as Default Settings above, plus Permission Required to gate the tier.

docs.title: UI
docs.text: Key Default Description Slots Shown Before Overflow Wrap 4 How many slots are shown before the preview wraps to an overflow +N indicator. Effect - Opening Safe Pocket (empty disables) assets/bundled/prefabs/fx/player/beartrap_clothing_rustle.prefab Effect played when opening starts. Empty string disables it. Effect - Safe Pocket Finished Opening (empty disables) assets/bundled/prefabs/fx/impacts/blunt/cloth/cloth1.prefab Effect played when opening finishes. Empty string disables it. Show Opening Progress Bar true Whether the animated fill bar shows during the opening delay. Button Position - Anchor X (0-1) 0.5 Anchor X (0–1) for the Safe Pocket button. Button Position - Anchor Y (0-1) 0 Anchor Y (0–1) for the Safe Pocket button. Button Position - Offset Left 532 Pixel offset left from the anchor point. Button Position - Offset Up 170 Pixel offset up from the anchor point. Show Button Title true Whether "SAFE POCKET" text shows above the button. Show Button Tooltip true Whether hovering the button shows the explanatory tooltip.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command Description safepocket.open (console command, bound to the UI button) Opens or closes the caller's Safe Pocket.

docs.title: WarMode
docs.text: Flag players as PVP or PVE. Controls what players can attack, loot, target, and mount based on their current mode. Ships with PVP, PVE, and NPC modes out of the box; fully custom modes can be added via the config or the Admin Panel extension.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Permission Effect warmode.admin Access to all admin commands (warmode.setplayer, warmode.setall, etc.).

Modes are backed by Oxide permission groups, not individual permissions. The group name for each mode is set in the config under Group (e.g. warmodepvp, warmodepve). Players in a mode's group will be assigned that mode on next login/mode resolution. When a player qualifies for multiple mode groups, the one with the lowest Priority value wins.

docs.title: Player commands
docs.text: Command Default Description /<flag command> /flag Toggle between available modes (cycles through Mode Options in config), or specify a mode name directly, e.g. /flag pvp. Configurable via Chat Command in the Flagging section.

docs.title: Admin commands (require warmode.admin)
docs.text: Command Arguments Description /warmode — Prints a list of all available admin commands. /warmode.setplayer <player> <mode> Sets the mode for the specified player by name or Steam ID. /warmode.setall <mode> Sets the mode for every player currently on the server. /warmode.mode [player] Displays the current mode for the given player, or your own if omitted. /warmode.tc — Displays the mode of the base (Tool Cupboard) you are currently standing in. /warmode.getmode — Displays the mode of the entity or player you are looking at. /warmode.debugmode [id] [mode\|clear] Assign a fake mode to any player ID for testing. Omit all args to clear all debug overrides. /wmc or /warmode.config — Opens the WarMode Admin Panel UI (requires WarMode Admin Panel extension).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Plugin integration sections (ZoneManager, RaidableBases, BetterChat, SimpleStatus, etc.) are hidden by default and only appear in the config once the relevant plugin is loaded. After installing a new integration plugin, reload WarMode and the new section will be written to your config automatically.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Key Default Description Initial Player Mode pvp Mode assigned to brand-new players on their first spawn. Npc Mode npc Mode assigned to NPC players spawned by other plugins. Vanilla scientists are not affected. Allow Vehicle Mode Ownership false When enabled, vehicles and horses owned by a player (via VehicleLicense or similar) are treated as claimedvehicles / claimedhorses rather than generic vehicles / horses, giving them separate rule entries. Always Allow Twig Damage true When true, twig building blocks can always be damaged regardless of mode rules. Always Allow Twig Placement false When true, twig placement is allowed inside any base regardless of mode rules. When false, players cannot place twig blocks in bases they could not otherwise attack. Can Kill Trespassing Sleepers false When true, players who log out inside another player's base can be killed regardless of their mode. Show Debug Messages In Console false Prints rule decision messages to the server console. Extremely spammy — only enable when debugging. Allow Plugin Override true When true, other plugins (Sputnik, Convoy, etc.) can override WarMode rules inside their own zones. When false, WarMode retains its own rules even inside third-party zones.

docs.title: Flagging
docs.text:
Controls the /flag command players use to switch their own mode.

Key Default Description Chat Command flag The chat command players type to change their mode. Mode Options ["pve", "pvp"] Which modes are available for players to cycle through with the flag command. Requires Safe Zone true Players must be inside a safe zone to use the flag command. If team sync is on, all active team members must be in a safe zone. Requires No Hostile true Players must not be marked as hostile. If team sync is on, all active team members must be non-hostile. Requires Team Leader false Only the team leader can use the flag command. Solo players are not affected. Cooldown Seconds 60 Seconds before the flag command can be used again. Set to 0 to disable the cooldown.

docs.title: Teams
docs.text: Key Default Description Sync Mode With Team Members true When a player's mode changes, all active team members are synced to the mode with the lowest priority among the team.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: Key Default Description Chat true Send mode change notifications via chat. Toastify false Send mode change notifications via Toastify (requires Toastify plugin).

docs.title: Chat
docs.text: Key Default Description Show Plugin Prefix true Prepends [WarMode] to plugin chat messages. Plugin Prefix Color #aaee32 Hex color for the [WarMode] prefix. Steam Id For Icon 0 Steam ID whose avatar is used as the chat icon for WarMode messages. Sfx Fail (keypad denied) Sound effect played for negative notifications. Sfx Success (keypad updated) Sound effect played for positive notifications.

docs.title: Marker
docs.text:
The crosshair marker that appears when a player aims their weapon at another player who has Show Marker When Aimed At enabled for their mode.

Key Default Description Show true Master toggle for all mode markers. Distance 100 Maximum distance (meters) at which the marker is visible. Update Interval 0.5 How often (seconds) the marker refreshes. Lower values are more responsive but may impact performance. Image assets/icons/peace.png Sprite asset path for the marker icon. Size 16 Marker icon size in pixels. Color 0 0 1 0 0.5 RGBA color of the marker.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
An array of mode objects. The three default modes are pvp, pve, and npc.

Key Default Description Name (required) Unique internal identifier for the mode (lowercase, no spaces). Used in all config rule arrays, commands, and API calls. Display Name (mode name uppercased) Name shown to players in chat messages. If blank, falls back to the localization key mode <name>. Color Hex (varies) Hex color used when the mode name is referenced in chat messages from WarMode itself. Group null Oxide permission group that places players into this mode. Required for player-usable modes; leave null for NPC-only modes. Priority null Lower number = higher precedence. When a player is in multiple mode groups (or team sync is active), the mode with the lowest priority wins. Required when Group is set. Show Marker When Aimed At true Whether the crosshair marker is shown when another player aims at someone in this mode. Always Allow Fire Damage false If true, fire/incendiary damage always applies to this player and their property, regardless of what mode caused it. Can Take Patrol Heli Damage true If false, patrol helicopters cannot damage players or bases of this mode. Deep Sea Mode "" Mode players automatically switch to when entering the deep sea. Leave blank to keep their current mode.

docs.title: Rule arrays
docs.text:
Each mode has five rule dictionaries — Can Attack Types, Can Loot Types, Can Target Types, Can Mount Types, and Can Enter Types. Each dictionary maps an entity category to an array of mode names that this mode is allowed to interact with.

Example: "Can Attack Types": { "players": ["pvp", "npc"] } means a player in this mode can attack players who are in pvp or npc mode.

Attacking entity categories:

Category Entities players Other players buildings Building blocks, doors, deployables, IO entities traps Bear traps, barricades, gun traps containers Storage boxes and similar containers turrets Auto turrets, flame turrets samsites SAM sites horses Unclaimed ridable horses vehicles Unclaimed vehicles (cars, helicopters, etc.) tugboats Tugboats and anything attached to them legacyshelters Legacy shelter entities claimedvehicles Player-owned vehicles (requires Allow Vehicle Mode Ownership) claimedhorses Player-owned horses (requires Allow Vehicle Mode Ownership) stashes Hidden stashes sleepingbags Sleeping bags and beds miningquarries Mining quarries and pump jacks modularboats Player-built modular boats

Looting entity categories: same as Attacking plus growables, droppedbackpacks, publiccontainers, droppeditems.

Targeting entity categories (traps, turrets, samsites auto-targeting): traps, turrets, samsites.

Mounting entity categories: vehicles, horses, tugboats, claimedvehicles, claimedhorses, modularboats.

Entering entity categories: claimedmonuments.

docs.title: ZoneManager (appears when ZoneManager is installed)
docs.text: Key Default Description Force Mode In Zone (example entries) Dictionary mapping zone selectors to mode names. Key format: <property><operator><value> where property is id or name, operator is = (exact) or ~ (partial). Example: "id=abc123" → "pvp" or "name~arena" → "pvp". Zone Exit Delay 3 Seconds to wait after a player leaves a forced zone before reverting their mode. Prevents rapid flickering near zone borders. Re-entering the zone during the delay cancels the revert. Set to 0 for immediate revert.

docs.title: Raidable Bases (appears when Raidable Bases is installed)
docs.text: Key Default Description Protection Radius 50 Must match the Protection Radius set in the Raidable Bases config. Can Enter Pvp Raidable Bases ["pvp"] Modes allowed to enter PVP raidable bases. Players in other modes are ejected. Can Enter Pve Raidable Bases ["pve", "pvp"] Modes allowed to enter PVE raidable bases. Forced Mode Pvp Zone → Forced Mode "" Mode players appear to be in while inside a PVP raidable base. Leave blank to not force a mode. Forced Mode Pve Zone → Forced Mode "" Mode players appear to be in while inside a PVE raidable base. Leave blank to not force a mode.

docs.title: BetterChat (appears when BetterChat is installed)
docs.text: Key Default Description Show Mode Prefix In Chat true Show the player's current mode as a title prefix in BetterChat. Modes → <mode> → Show Mode Title In Chat true Whether this mode's title appears in chat for players who hold it. Modes → <mode> → Mode Title Format [{0}] Format string for the mode title. {0} is replaced with the mode's display name.

docs.title: SimpleStatus (appears when SimpleStatus is installed)
docs.text: Key Default Description Mode Status Bars → <mode> → Show true Whether the status bar for this mode is displayed. Mode Status Bars → <mode> → Background Color (varies) RGBA background color of the status bar. Mode Status Bars → <mode> → Image (varies) Sprite asset path for the status bar icon. Only sprites are currently supported. Mode Status Bars → <mode> → Image Color (varies) RGBA tint color applied to the icon. Mode Status Bars → <mode> → Title Color (varies) RGBA color of the mode title text in the status bar. Mode Status Bars → <mode> → Text Color (varies) RGBA color of the subtitle text in the status bar.

docs.title: NoEscape (appears when NoEscape is installed)
docs.text: Key Default Description Prevent Flagging While Combat Blocked true Players cannot use the flag command while combat blocked. Prevent Flagging While Raid Blocked true Players cannot use the flag command while raid blocked. Prevent Flagging While Escape Blocked true Players cannot use the flag command while escape blocked.

docs.title: Toastify (appears when Toastify is installed)
docs.text: Key Default Description Positive Toast ID success Toast type ID for positive mode notifications. Must match a toast defined in your Toastify config. Negative Toast ID error Toast type ID for negative/blocked notifications. Duration 4 How long (seconds) toasts remain visible.

docs.title: Event plugin forced modes (each section appears when the respective plugin is installed)
docs.text:
Each supported event plugin has its own config section containing a single key:

Key Default Description Forced Mode pvp Mode players appear to be in while inside that plugin's event zone. Leave blank ("") to not force a mode.

docs.title: Hooks (callable by other plugins)
docs.text:
// Called whenever a player's effective mode changes, or when config is reloaded.
// userid: the player's Steam ID string
// modeId: the mode's internal Name (e.g. "pvp", "pve")
private void WarMode_PlayerModeUpdated(string userid, string modeId) { }

// Return false to prevent a player from using the /flag command.
// Return null or true to allow it.
private object WarMode_CanUseFlagCommand(string userid) { }

// Called when the flag command is about to execute.
// Return a non-null value to cancel WarMode's default mode-switching logic
// (e.g. if your plugin is handling it).
private object WarMode_OnFlagCommand(string userid, string requestedMode) { }

docs.title: Methods (callable on the WarMode plugin reference)
docs.text:
// Returns the internal mode name of an entity, taking forced zones into account.
string GetEntityMode(BaseEntity entity);

// Returns the Oxide group name for a given mode id (e.g. "pve" → "warmodepve").
string GetModeGroup(string modeId);

// Returns the target-type category name for an entity (e.g. "players", "buildings").
string GetEntityTargetType(BaseEntity entity);

docs.title: Extension plugins
docs.text: Plugin Description WarMode Admin Panel In-game UI for editing modes, rules, settings, zones, players, and event plugin forced modes. Opens with /wmc. WarMode Badges Displays a configurable HUD badge showing each player's current mode. WarMode Rules UI In-game rules board that shows players what the PVP/PVE rules are on the server. WarMode Spawn UI Selection screen shown to new players so they can choose their starting mode.
